label: L=9 copy step 11 (output orig[2]) when first two tokens are a specific pair
explanation: Very sparse, weak reset-gate unit (max activation 0.005). Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely in length-9 sequences at t=11 (two steps after <DEL>, input = orig[1], output = orig[2]): that one position holds 94% of activation mass and covers 91% of activations, but only about 2% of such steps fire. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, nor in sequences of length <= 7. Which of those steps fire depends on token identity: the current input (orig[1]) being r/s/x/3/f/v and the previous input (orig[0]) being 1/q/3/j/p/f; top activations are pairs like f-x, q-r, 1-f, 1-s, 3-3. More digits in the sequence raise the firing rate. The token-pair predicate gets dev F1 about 0.38 (precision 0.30, recall 0.53, mass recall 0.63), so the token selectivity is only partly captured. The largest activations are best covered (69% of the top quartile).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+3.30), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.30), prev_tok=1 (+2.40), prev_tok=j (+2.25), next_out=h (+2.18), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+2.13). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.70), n_digits=0 (-2.21), orig5=b (-1.73), next_out=- (-1.70).
